correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge3\), the five automorphism classes exhaust all unordered two-leader sets, and connectedness makes each grounded Laplacian invertible. The Sherman–Morrison reduction, direct symbolic reconstruction of five rational costs, and exact positive-coefficient expansions prove strict optimality of DD only at \(n=3\) and SS at every \(n\ge4\). The script verify.py replayed 1947 independent symbolic and direct-spectrum checks; the symbolic coefficients, not the bounded sweep, certify the infinite-domain sign claims. Modal Lyapunov equations independently verify the stationary second-order position covariance normalization. All boundary cases and optimizer multiplicities are included.

originality.rationale: Exact source- and object-specific comparisons separate the inverse-square grounded-Laplacian leader problem from published first-order inverse-trace results on the same one-link-defective biclique, and from inverse-square results on unmodified bipartite graphs. In particular the first-order known \(n=6\) switch does not imply the proved \(n=4\) switch: the cost rankings differ at \(n=4\),5. No accessible indexed statement yielded the exact inverse-square theorem. The full texts of particularly close indexed records were inaccessible, so an unindexed or hidden equivalent is a stated novelty risk, not asserted impossible.
residual_risks: Three related published indexed records had readable detailed summaries but inaccessible complete repository texts; equivalences in their uninspected parts cannot be conclusively excluded.
Unindexed or differently named publications may state an inverse-square missing-edge leader theorem.
A database search and graph-family specialization do not establish uniqueness of the result in the full literature.

value.rationale: The failure of one intercommunity link is a minimal natural fault-tolerance setting, and second-order matched velocity/position consensus has a physically motivated inverse-square covariance objective. The new complete optimizer classification shows an exact order-sensitive design transition at \(n=4\), strictly conflicting with the established first-order placement at \(n=4\) and \(n=5\). This is a structural, every-network-size decision rule with nontrivial five-orbit proof, not an isolated table entry, a reparametrization, or a routine numerical lookup.
